cohort: The study included term pregnant women (>= 37 weeks, singleton, cephalic presentation) requesting epidural analgesia.
finding: Walking epidural analgesia (WEA) is an effective and safe alternative to conventional epidural analgesia, allowing significantly better ambulation (91% unassisted) without significant differences in obstetric outcomes or neonatal well-being compared to CEA.
mod_finding: No differences were observed in mode of delivery between the WEA and CEA groups, with most pregnancies resulting in vaginal delivery in both groups.
country: N/A (Clinica Universitaria Reina Fabiola (CURF) is mentioned, but the country is not specified in the abstract.)
